name: OK-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+28 partisan lean anchors the district firmly in Republican hands
Incumbent Brecheen holds an overwhelming fundraising edge ($219k raised vs. $4.3k)
No public polling; challenger Wade has only $86 on hand
model.rationale: An R+28 district with a running incumbent facing a challenger who has raised $4,290 and holds $86 leaves no visible competitive path, and prediction markets price the Republican at 98%. The expected margin sits around 22 points Republican, consistent with the district's structural lean plus modest incumbency and money advantages.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Brecheen or an unexpected scandal would be the only plausible source of movement in this safely Republican seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Oklahoma's 2nd District is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 28 points to the GOP. Incumbent Josh Brecheen is seeking re-election and faces Democrat Brandon Wade and independent Ronnie Hopkins in the general election. No public polls of the race are available, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive.

The financial picture is lopsided: Brecheen has raised about $219,000 and holds $76,000 on hand, while Wade has raised roughly $4,300 with just $86 remaining. Prediction markets give Brecheen a 98% chance of winning. With the district's structural lean, the incumbent's advantages, and a challenger showing minimal campaign activity, the race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin of about 22 points.
